record.method: Homogenisation of the Green function at all scales plus the DGFF argument.
record.obstruction: The analogue of the cluster law is environment-dependent; the statement of Theorem 9.3 must be modified before it can be proved.
record.result: The quenched Green function of the random conductance model in d=2 is g_eff log|x-y| + O(1) up to the scale where homogenisation holds; the concentric decomposition needs the O(1) error to be controlled uniformly over all dyadic scales near a point, which is a quenched local limit theorem at every scale. This is available for uniformly elliptic ergodic conductances by Andres-Deuschel-Slowik type estimates for the heat kernel, so the intermediate level sets (which only need two-point covariances) follow the DGFF proof with g replaced by g_eff. The extremal-process cluster law, however, depends on the local geometry of the conductances around the maximiser and is therefore itself random (not a constant law), which changes the STATEMENT of the Theorem 9.3 analogue: the cluster law becomes a random law indexed by the environment at the maximiser. This suggests the problem as posed needs reformulation for the extremal process.

record.exclusion_reason: Later2025 random-conductance field/Green convergence must be compared to the exact microscopic covariance and rare-level target before admission.
